newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Oil Co of Australia eyes gas field.
newsitem.headline: Oil Co of Australia eyes gas field.

text.p: Oil Co of Australia Ltd, a subsidiary of Boral Ltd, said on Tuesday it had launched its first commercial venture into coal seam gas recovery through a proposed acquisition of a 50 percent interest in a southeast Queensland coal seam gas field.
The company said in a statement it believed coal seam gas was the emerging supply source for natural gas and it was committed to developing it as a viable commercial energy source.
It said it had reached an agreement in principle to acquire a 50 percent working interest in the ATP 525P field, located about 120 km east of the town of Roma.

Under the agreement, Oil Co of Australia said it will acquire part of an interest currently held by Pacific Oil & Gas Pty Ltd, wholly-owned unit RTZ-CRA, and will buy interests held by QGAS Pty Ltd and GFK Investment Pty Ltd.
Once the transaction is completed, Oil Co of Australia and Pacific Oil & Gas would each hold 50 percent, the company said.
The cost of the acquisition was not disclosed.

"Eastern Australia's current reserves of conventional natural gas are already committed to existing users," the company's general manager, Paul Elkington, said in the statement. "It is generally accepted that potentially, Queensland's coal seam methane reserves far exceed available conventional natural gas supplies, and tapping them will open up significant new development opportunities," he said.
